questions.question: Who among the following built the Hawa Mahal in Jaipur?
questions.solution: Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh built the Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds) in 1799. It features 953 small windows (Jharokhas).

questions.question: Which among the following rulers adopted the title devaputra?
questions.solution: Kushana rulers adopted the title Devaputra (Son of God), likely influenced by Chinese rulers who called themselves Sons of Heaven.

questions.question: Four ashrams were recognised by Brahmins around the time when Jainism and Buddhism were becoming popular. Which of the following was NOT a recognised ashrama?
questions.solution: Parmarth is not a recognized ashrama. The four stages of life are: Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, and Sannyasa.

questions.question: The founder of Brahmo Sabha was _________.
questions.solution: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which later became the Brahmo Samaj, focusing on monotheism and social reform.

questions.question: The Amaravati School of art was developed under the patronage of _________.
questions.solution: Satavahanas patronized the Amaravati School of Art in Andhra Pradesh. Style: Use of white marble and focus on narrative sculptures of Buddha's life.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, what is the total literacy rate in India (approximately)?
questions.solution: 74% (exactly 74.04%) was the total literacy rate according to the 2011 Census. Male: 82.14%, Female: 65.46%.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Dharma Sabha?
questions.solution: Radhakanta Deb founded the Dharma Sabha in 1830. Fact: It was an orthodox society formed to oppose the abolition of Sati.

questions.question: Who promoted the worship of God in Punjab, India as Nirankar (Formless)?
questions.solution: Baba Dayal Das was the founder of the Nirankari Movement, emphasizing the worship of God as 'Nirankar' (the formless one).

questions.question: Who built the Red Fort in Delhi?
questions.solution: Shah Jahan built the Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi after shifting his capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad.

questions.question: Sultan Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraja III in ________.
questions.solution: 1192 was the year Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at the Second Battle of Tarain. Result: Establishment of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: Annie Besant laid the foundation of the Central Hindu College in ________ in 1898 where both Hindu religion and Western scientific subjects were taught.
questions.solution: Banaras is where Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College, which later formed the nucleus of the Banaras Hindu University (BHU).

questions.question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from ________.
questions.solution: <u>Queen Elizabeth I</u> granted the Royal Charter to the East India Company on December 31, 1600, giving them a monopoly on trade with the East.

questions.question: Which of the following ancient site is NOT situated in India?
questions.solution: Mehrgarh is located in present-day Balochistan, Pakistan. It is one of the earliest sites showing evidence of farming and herding.

questions.question: Around 2000 years ago ________ became the second capital of the Kushanas.
questions.solution: Mathura became the second capital of the Kushanas under Kanishka. Their first capital was Purushpura (Peshawar).

questions.question: The objective of Simon Commission was to _______.
questions.solution: decide India's Political future was the purpose of the Simon Commission (appointed in 1927). It was boycotted because it had no Indian members.

questions.question: Which of the following architecture is a memorial of Aurangzeb's wife, Dilras Banu Begum?
questions.solution: Bibi Ka Maqbara (Aurangabad) is the tomb of Dilras Banu Begum. It is often called the 'Taj of the Deccan' due to its resemblance to the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: The Ilbert Bill provided for ______.
questions.option_2: Equality between British and Indian Judges
questions.solution: <u>Equality between British and Indian Judges</u> was the main provision of the Ilbert Bill, which allowed Indian sessions judges to try Europeans.

questions.question: Alivardi Khan was followed by ______ as the Nawab of Bengal.
questions.solution: Sirajuddaulah became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756. Battle: He fought the British in the Battle of Plassey (1757).

questions.question: What happened in Bengal, India, in 1770 that resulted in the death of one-third of the population?
questions.solution: <u>Famine</u> (The Great Bengal Famine of 1770) killed about 10 million people, nearly one-third of the population of Bengal.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Widow Remarriage Association (1861)?
questions.solution: Mahadev Govind Ranade (M.G. Ranade) founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1861. He is known as the 'Socrates of Maharashtra'.

questions.question: After years of wandering Babur seized Kabul in _______.
questions.solution: <u>1504</u> was the year Babur conquered Kabul, which became his base before invading India.

questions.question: The famous Sheesh Mahal in Punjab was built by which of the following rulers?
questions.solution: <u>Maharaja Narinder Singh</u> of Patiala built the Sheesh Mahal (Palace of Mirrors) in the 19th century.

questions.question: When was the Dev Samaj founded in Lahore by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri?
questions.solution: 1887 was when the Dev Samaj was founded. It emphasized the eternity of the soul and the importance of good moral conduct.

questions.question: Badruddin Tyabji addressed the congress as president in _______.
questions.solution: 1887 (Madras Session) is when Badruddin Tyabji became the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress.

questions.question: Mohenjodaro belongs to which of the following civilization?
questions.solution: Indus Valley civilization (Harappan Civilization) included Mohenjodaro, which means 'Mound of the Dead'.
